evidence_summary: Effects Database identifies the Hohner MF-50 as Hohner by Shin-Ei; Tone Machines dates the Hohner version to late 1973 or early 1974 and places it in Shin-Ei's Super Fuzz OEM network. Hohner remains the marketed identity, Shin-Ei the builder relationship.
Hohner MF-50 is explicitly linked to the Shin-Ei Companion FY-6 OEM family; related marketed states remain separate records rather than being merged into Hohner.

Effects Database places Hohner FW-10 Dirty Wah'er in the Applied FW-3 OEM family; the related Applied FW-3 record identifies U.S. manufacture by Applied Audio and Hohner FW-10 as a marketed descendant/state.

Tone Machines documents Applied Audio's 1977 reintroduction of the Shin-Ei-derived Surf Wah under Hohner as the ME-30 Multi-Exciter; Effects Database links the Hohner ME-30 to the Applied/Guild SP-5 and Shin-Ei ME-7 family.

Effects Database related-family mapping places Hohner WW-20 within Applied's wah OEM line, but model-specific historical documentation is thinner than for FW-10 and ME-30; retain as candidate rather than full public promotion.

Tone Machines states Hohner later connected with Applied Audio and that Applied built a full Sound Modifier line, including the Tri-Dirty Booster. Specific models should still carry their own evidence rather than inheriting one blanket factory label.

Newer specialist research identifies Applied Audio Products as the later Hohner effects contractor, while earlier references only established an unknown U.S. third-party factory. Archive now records Applied as a high-confidence builder attribution, while preserving prior uncertainty in the evidence trail.
